title: AI consulting services: is it worth it, and what does it cost?
description: What AI consulting should deliver, what it costs against hiring a team or buying software, and the work where AI pays first. With our own data.
summary: AI consulting should take one costly job off your team, such as invoice exceptions, which hit about 1 invoice in 5[^31]. Most generative AI never shows up in profit[^1][^13]. Winners benchmark on their own files[^5] and budget for after launch, where most of the cost sits[^3][^9].
verdict: Hire AI help for one problem with a number attached, not a strategy deck[^1][^12].
Buy or partner before you build: bought projects succeed about 3 times as often[^1], and most are now bought[^2].
Benchmark the options on your own files before anyone builds[^5][^20].
Our AI Sprint costs $10,000 for 30 days, about a month of one data scientist's median pay[^18][^4].
Re-check the model each year: AI keeps getting cheaper[^19], and running it is most of the cost[^3].

pickElse: AI is your product and you will run many systems: hire in-house. Technical roles take a median 75 days to fill[^17], so budget for that and the pay in the table above[^4][^14].

A standard job that software already does, such as accounts payable: buy the product and benchmark it on your own files. 76% of enterprise AI use cases are now bought[^2], and bought projects succeed about 3 times as often as internal builds[^1].

spokes.why: Accounts payable: reading invoices is the easy part, but about 1 in 5 (19.9%) hit an exception, a mismatch someone must fix[^31]. The money is in those exceptions and in payments fraud, which 76% of US firms faced in 2025[^32].
Reading PDFs, scans and forms. Our sealed benchmark found two models with zero mistakes on 30 fund reports[^6].
If you lend or insure: AI does the reading so underwriters spend their time on the decision, which must stay explainable[^21][^26].

If you lend: score loans with a model you can explain, and add a stronger, harder-to-explain one only if your benchmark shows lift[^33]. Stronger models usually score higher, but the gap narrows on small data[^33], and every decline needs specific reasons[^21][^22].

ownData.intro: These are US median pay figures from the Bureau of Labor Statistics for May 2025[^4][^14]. AI job titles have no BLS group of their own, so each row uses the nearest one. A lean team of one manager, one data scientist and one developer costs about $630,000 a year with benefits[^16].

Cost with benefits divides median pay by 68.5%, the wage share of pay costs for full-time private workers in June 2026[^16]. Medians cover all employers and experience levels, not one specific hire.

example.input: A mid-sized lender wants AI to read small-business loan files so underwriters stop spreading bank statements and tax returns by hand. Spreading means retyping their numbers into the lender's standard analysis sheet.
example.output: A benchmark of the leading models on 50 of the lender's own files, with the cost per file for each. Today's time and error rate per file sit next to the winner's. The winner goes into the loan system with a review queue for unsure cases, and is re-checked monthly as new models ship.

recipesTitle: How should a good AI consulting engagement run?

recipes.name: 1. Benchmark first
recipes.when: Before anyone builds, to settle which approach wins on your files and what it costs; public leaderboards are only a first filter[^5]. Pick a high-volume, repetitive job with a known cost of errors, and price it today: an invoice costs $9.90 on average to process[^31].
flow: Process lead: measure today's time and error rate per file
Your team: agree the right answers, then lock them
Consultant: report accuracy and cost per file
recipes.cost: Quoted per job, with a fixed scope. Make sure you keep the files, the answer key and the code, so you can re-run it.

recipes.name: 2. Build the winner into the work
recipes.when: Once the benchmark shows a clear winner that pays back.
flow: Consultant: set up the winning model
IT: connect it to your systems and workflow
Named reviewer: clear the queue of unsure cases
Process lead: go live at one site or team first
Process lead: move to full volume
recipes.cost: Depends on the systems it touches. Gartner warns that a production system can cost many times the pilot[^3][^9], so scope it from the benchmark, not the demo.

recipes.name: 3. Keep it right
recipes.when: Always, because models, prices and your documents change. The same AI performance gets 9 to 900 times cheaper each year[^19].
flow: Consultant: flag a new model or price change
Process lead: check if it's cheaper or better
You: decide to switch, or keep
recipes.cost: Small, because the benchmark already exists. Running the model is at least 70% of its lifetime cost[^3][^9], so a cheaper model that passes the benchmark saves on every file.

testTitle: How do you benchmark whether a consultant can deliver?
howToTest: Measure today first, so the after has a before.
Ask for a benchmark on 20 to 50 of your own files before you sign for a full build.
Agree the right answers with your own team first, and lock them, so the result is graded against your standard.
Ask for cost per correct answer, not price per token. In our benchmark the cheapest tool made 16 wrong answers; the two best made none[^7].
Ask why they picked their model. In our benchmark, two tools found nearly the same facts at prices 48 times apart[^7]; Claude's own list prices span about 40 times[^8].
Ask what happens when a better model ships next month. If the answer is a new project, the system will go stale.
Ask for a client where the system has run in production for at least six months.
Ask where your files are stored, who can see them, and whether anyone trains AI models on them.
If you lend or insure, ask what model documentation and validation you get for your examiner, and who keeps it current.
Ask who clears unsure cases, how fast, and who covers when they're out.

buyVsBuild.buy: Hire a consultant when you need one system working this quarter, have no AI engineers, and want someone accountable for the result. Pay for a fixed scope with a benchmark you can check. Bought or partnered projects succeed about 3 times as often as internal builds[^1].
buyVsBuild.build: Hire in-house when AI is core to what you sell and you will run many systems. Expect about two and a half months to fill each technical role[^17] and the pay in the table above[^4][^14].

watchOuts: Firms that resell one software vendor's product and call it a recommendation. 37% of enterprise CIOs surveyed by a16z run five or more models, picked by use case[^5].
Demos on clean sample data that never meet your real files. Gartner lists poor data quality among the main reasons generative AI projects are dropped after the proof of concept[^10].
No answer key: without agreed right answers, nobody can show the system works. Anthropic's own guide says to set measurable success criteria and benchmark on cases that mirror the real task[^20].
Budgets that stop at the pilot. Gartner expects at least half of generative AI projects to overrun through 2028, and running the model is most of the lifetime cost[^3][^9].

offer.heading: Not sure where AI pays in your business? Get a free diagnostic
offer.body: Bring one job with a number attached. In 30 minutes you leave knowing which job to start with, whether to buy or build, and what to benchmark first. You talk to the person who does the work, not a sales team.

rules.name: AI credit scoring: the lending rules
rules.status: US in force; EU from 2 Dec 2027
rules.what: If you lend, US rules require a decline notice within 30 days, giving the specific reasons or how to ask for them[^21]. Those reasons must be the factors the model actually scored[^22]. In the EU, credit scoring of people becomes a high-risk AI use from 2 December 2027[^23][^24][^25].

rules.name: AI underwriting: the insurance rules
rules.status: US in force; EU from 2 Dec 2027
rules.what: If you insure, New York expects and Colorado requires testing AI and outside data for unfair discrimination[^26][^29][^30]. 30 jurisdictions expect a written AI program with vendor oversight[^27][^28]. In the EU, life and health insurance pricing becomes a high-risk AI use from 2 December 2027[^23][^24][^25].
